title: In Serbia’s 2026 election, 38,286 votes won no seat and 12,348 votes won one
body: On 25 October 2026 Serbia elected the 250 members of its National Assembly, and President Aleksandar Vučić conceded defeat to the student-led list that night, [Reuters reported](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2026/10/26/serbia039s-vucic-concedes-defeat-to-student-led-movement-in-parliamentary-election). The country is one constituency and seats go by the d’Hondt method: each list’s votes are divided by 1, 2, 3 and so on, and the 250 highest numbers win seats. Only lists with 3% of the votes cast take part, about 128,000 in the [preliminary count](https://www.novosti.rs/vesti/politika/1664282/najnoviji-presek-oglasio-rik-obradjeno-8-136-birackih-mesta), so the Authentic Right’s 38,286 won nothing. National-minority lists are the exception: under [article 140 of the election law](https://www.te.gob.mx/vota_elections/thesaurus/article/50488/16592/175) they take part with any number of votes, and under 3% their quotients are raised by 35%. That lifted SDA Sandžak’s 12,348 votes to 16,670, just above the 16,046 the 250th seat cost: four minority lists shared 6 seats, the Student List took 140 and United Serbia 104.

slides.prompt: Serbia, 25 October 2026: the Authentic Right list got 38,286 votes, the SDA Sandžak list 12,348. Which of them won a seat?
slides.detail: A list needs 3% of the votes cast, about 128,000, to take part in the sharing of seats, unless it is a national-minority list: those skip the line, and their quotients are raised by 35%.

slides.alt: Animation on midnight blue: a fan of 250 seats, bars for Serbia’s lists with a gold 3% line, ladders of d’Hondt quotients around the 250th number, a minority list’s quotient lifted by 1.35, then the chamber filling with 140, 104 and 6 seats.
slides.music: “Son of a Rocket” Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com) · CC BY 4.0

slides.prompt: Give your own list the fewest votes that still win it a seat. Try it as an ordinary list, then as a national-minority list.
slides.takeaway: As a minority list, about 12,000 votes buy a seat: they skip the 3% line and are multiplied by 1.35. As an ordinary list you need 3% of the votes cast, about 128,000, before the count even begins.

slides.question: In Serbia’s 2026 election, why did 12,348 votes for SDA Sandžak win a seat while 38,286 votes for the Authentic Right won none?
options: SDA ran in a district with fewer voters
The Authentic Right withdrew its list
Votes under 3% go to the biggest list
slides.explanation: Serbia is one constituency. A list needs 3% of the votes cast to take part, unless it is a national-minority list; those take part anyway, and under 3% their d’Hondt quotients are raised by 35%.
